subject: Next steps — embed & rerank POC, SDK changes and handoff
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@cortexinc.com>, Anika Shah <anika@cortexinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — embed & rerank POC, SDK changes and handoff

Hi Oliver / Anika —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our side plus the concrete next steps so we don’t lose momentum. I’ve attached a one-page requirements summary (cortex-mpa-embed-reqs.pdf) and a tentative scope spreadsheet (proto-scope-v1.xlsx).

Key pain / goals (what you emphasized):
- Tight latencies for real-time recommendation UI (~50–100ms server-side target)
- Ranked embeddings for cross-document retrieval, ~1M docs initially
- Deterministic behaviour for rerank scores (auditability + predictable A/Bing)
- Minimal infra changes on Cortex side — prefer SDK + small adaptor to keep latency predictable

What Redwood proposes for the POC:
1) Embed flow for ingestion and online lookups using our embedding API + a simple vector store prototype (we’ll provide a reference adaptor).
2) Rerank step after recall: small streaming reranker call (stream tokens -> early scores) to hit the latency window.
3) SDK change request: we’ll ship a lightweight SDK patch that exposes an async streaming funcall and a small structured-output schema for the reranker response. Priyom will own the patch.
4) Ops handoff: Ben / Marissa to draft an acceptance checklist and a rollback plan (canary traffic split to baseline model).

Immediate next steps (owners & dates):
- Redwood: share embed/rerank proto repo + SDK patch by Wed EOD (Priyom)
- Cortex: share sample dataset / expected QPS profile and the doc store details by Thu EOD (Oliver)
- Joint: 30-min technical sync next Tue (Oct 12) — aim to run first micro-benchmark after SDK patch

Open questions we flagged:
- Will Cortex host vector store or prefer Redwood-managed cache? (affects SLOs)
- Acceptable fallback when reranker times out (we suggested scoring-based fallback to coarse ranking)

If that aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite for the tech sync and Priyom will post the repo link to the Drive folder.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: cortex-mpa-embed-reqs.pdf (1 page), proto-scope-v1.xlsx (workbook)
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@cortexinc.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Anika Shah <anika@cortexinc.com>, eng+infra@cortexinc.com
Date: Mon, 4 Oct 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — embed & rerank POC, SDK changes and handoff

Irene —

Appreciate the succinct notes. This matches our internal takeaways. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can tolerate up to ~120ms server-side if the front-end does some progressive reveal; 50–100ms is preferred but 120ms is workable for phase 1.
- We’ll host the vector store ourselves (Postgres + PGVector) but would like Redwood to provide a small adaptor where you can return embeddings with metadata that we then upsert.
- Fallback strategy: prefer to use the embedding recall score when reranker times out; that’s acceptable.

I’ll upload a 10k-sample export to the Drive folder by Wed morning; Anika will share QPS numbers.

One ask: can the SDK patch be non-breaking for our current ingest pipeline? We can schedule a short upgrade window but avoiding breaking changes would speed the POC.

Thanks —
Oliver
Oliver Grant | Head of Product, Cortex Inc.

Folks —

Thanks — I’ll start the SDK patch this afternoon. Notes on approach and assumptions so we’re explicit:
- SDK: add an async streaming func call (redwood.streaming.rerank) that yields structured score objects (id, score, tokens_consumed). Expose a non-streaming wrapper for convenience.
- Backwards compatibility: the changes will be additive only. No existing calls will be mutated. We’ll bump minor version and include a migration guide.
- Resource usage: local dev build will default to a small kv-cache; we’ll include instrs to disable caching for Cortex’s Postgres setup.
- Test plan: unit tests + a simple end-to-end sample that upserts embeddings -> issues recall -> calls reranker. I’ll post test artifacts to the Drive link.

Planned deliverables and dates:
- Wed EOD: PR & demo script posted to Drive
- Thu: cross-team install & smoke test (1 hour)
- Next Tue: micro-benchmark with 10k sample

Putting Ben and Marissa on the thread to prepare the acceptance checklist and canary policy. I’ll call out any unexpected API constraints ASAP.

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Senior SDK Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick ops notes and next steps from our side:

Acceptance checklist (draft):
- Successful upsert of 10k sample into Cortex Postgres + PGVector (Cortex)
- Redwood SDK patch runs end-to-end against dev stack without errors (Redwood)
- Micro-benchmark: p95 end-to-end rerank latency <= 120ms for the test profile
- Canary plan: 5% traffic to POC model for 48 hours, auto-rollback on error rate > 2%

Rollout & contacts:
- On smoke test day, call in: infra-syn@redwood.com (ops channel)
- If we need a temporary config for deterministic rerank scoring, Priyom will push a param and Marissa will coordinate QA validation

Irene — please go ahead and send calendar invite for Tue Oct 12 10:00 AM PT for the technical sync. Oliver — thanks for committing the sample dataset; once available I’ll update the checklist to reflect exact numbers.

Ben Carter | Sr. Technical Program Manager, Redwood Inference
